title: Silver Strike Bowling
headline: Set the line. Roll. Watch the room react.
intro: Silver Strike compresses the bowling alley into a shared trackball and screen: choose a bowler and ball, line up, roll, then watch the pins settle while everyone judges the next shot. Classic player guidance describes a backswing followed by a forward roll — not a forward-only flick. The social payoff is the strike, the difficult spare and the running scoreboard; the 2009 kit also documents Series, Throwdown, Survivor and optional Vegas Bowling formats.

referenceScope.primary: Silver Strike Bowling 2009 (classic landscape offline kit)
referenceScope.reason: The 2009 kit manual is the most detailed primary source for this family's exact button labels and scoring rules; this build's own research already treats the classic offline game as a sourcing path distinct from the League Night reboot.
referenceScope.caveat: No release is selected or running here. The gallery's 2004 flyer predates the 2009 kit manual. Practical swing/setup tips come from an older community guide, not a verified 2009 playthrough; they are identified below and require a selected-release check.

session.format: Single 10-frame games, a 3-game Series, bracketed Throwdown contests for 4, 8 or 16 players, 3-Frame Practice, or Survivor (elimination on missed strikes); up to eight players are documented able to play together on one cabinet.
session.social: Players pick a male or female bowler and a ball weight before stepping up, then rotate through the same trackball panel while the lane, scoreboard and every other player's pin action stay on one shared screen between rolls.
session.failureToAvoid: Mounting the trackball too close to the screen risks a full forward-roll follow-through striking the monitor glass — the exact failure the manufacturer's own install guidance exists to prevent.

playLoop.title: Choose the session
playLoop.action: Choose an available format: a single game, a three-game Series, or an operator-enabled alternative such as Throwdown or Survivor.
playLoop.feedback: The selected format determines the scoring and elimination rules; availability depends on the cabinet's configuration.
playLoop.skill: Match the session to the group: a quick game and an elimination contest create different hand-off rhythms.

playLoop.title: Pick a bowler, ball and approach
playLoop.action: Choose a bowler and ball weight. An older community guide recommends holding Overhead while positioning the approach; verify that procedure on the selected release.
playLoop.feedback: The flyer shows the bowler-selection screen and a Spare Difficulty setting. Ball weight is a documented panel control, not a separate physical ball.
playLoop.skill: Make setup deliberate instead of accidentally starting the throw while repositioning.

playLoop.title: Draw back, then roll forward
playLoop.action: Use a controlled backswing and forward roll. The community guide warns that omitting the backswing produces a slow, weak ball; this is not a certified 2009 input specification.
playLoop.feedback: Watch the ball's path and pin action. The same guide recommends experimenting with hook and speed rather than simply rolling harder.
playLoop.skill: Repeat a useful gesture, then adjust one part of the setup at a time.

playLoop.title: Read the leave
playLoop.action: After the first ball, judge the remaining pins and plan the spare rather than repeating the same attempt.
playLoop.feedback: The lane and frame-by-frame scoreboard keep the result visible to the group; the archived flyer includes a dedicated spare screen.
playLoop.skill: Turn the result of one roll into the next decision.

playLoop.title: Chase the marks
playLoop.action: Continue through the game or configured contest. If Vegas Bowling is enabled, marks also feed its playing-card side game.
playLoop.feedback: The 2009 manual describes cards awarded for marks; Survivor instead eliminates players who fail to strike.
playLoop.skill: Choose whether the group wants score chasing, a side game or an escalating elimination contest.

screenRead.label: PLR1/PLR2 scoreboard strip
screenRead.meaning: Running frame-by-frame score for every player at the table, shown across the top during lane play.

screenRead.label: Spare Difficulty readout
screenRead.meaning: An on-screen handicap value set at bowler-select, letting a newer player pick an easier spare conversion before frame one.

screenRead.label: Ball-weight (lbs) indicator
screenRead.meaning: Shows the currently selected ball weight, one of five selectable weights documented by the manufacturer.

screenRead.label: Mark card (Vegas Bowling)
screenRead.meaning: When Vegas Bowling is enabled, every spare or strike draws a playing card; the best poker hand from the marks earned becomes a side competition layered on the score.

signatureMoments.title: The mark earns a card
signatureMoments.description: Every spare or strike interrupts the lane view with its own full-screen callout — SPARE, STRIKE, or an X-X Double graphic — turning ordinary scoring into a small event on its own before Vegas Bowling's card draw even happens.

signatureMoments.title: Drawing for the double
signatureMoments.description: Vegas Bowling turns every strike or spare into a card draw toward the best poker hand across the game — a side competition built directly into the software, not a house rule laid on top of it.

signatureMoments.title: Eight players, one lane
signatureMoments.description: Design interpretation: with up to eight players documented able to play together on one cabinet, a full session plays more like a pub bowling night passing one ball around than a solo arcade run.

controls.action: The older community guide describes a backswing followed by a forward roll, and a weak ball when the backswing is omitted. Confirm its exact behavior on the selected release.
controls.feel: Preserve motion in both directions and leave room for follow-through; the manufacturer's manual explicitly warns against hands hitting the monitor.

controls.action: Documented setup controls. The inspected installation manual does not establish a spin algorithm from these button names alone.
controls.feel: Keep the buttons distinct from the trackball; verify their in-play and menu behavior on the selected build before labeling a custom panel.

controls.action: Selects ball weight; the 2007 Bowler's Club manual labels this control Change Ball. The older community guide describes changing weight during play, so it should not be assumed to be a pre-game-only control.
controls.feel: A reachable setup control; exact timing and behavior belong in the selected-release check.

controls.action: The community guide describes holding it while positioning the approach and pressing it to reset a mistaken backswing. The installation manual confirms the control, not a between-frame-only camera restriction.
controls.feel: Keep it reachable during shot setup; check the reported modifier/reset behavior on the selected release.

controls.action: The kit documents Start as a separate input. An older player guide also reports a backswing-reset use; it does not establish Golden Tee's Skip Turn menu as a Silver Strike feature.
controls.feel: Verify start, selection and reset behavior independently; do not copy another game's menu mapping.

buildPriorities.title: Mount the trackball for a real follow-through
buildPriorities.why: The manufacturer's own install guidance exists specifically to keep a full forward roll's follow-through off the monitor glass.
buildPriorities.proof: A full forward follow-through completes with clearance between the player's hand and the screen.

buildPriorities.title: Keep the panel label generation-correct
buildPriorities.why: The ball-selection button's text differs by release (Ball Weight vs. Change Ball); mislabeling the panel misrepresents which software generation is actually running.
buildPriorities.proof: The physical button legend matches the exact software release installed, not a generic Silver Strike template.

buildPriorities.title: Ground the trackball separately from signal wiring
buildPriorities.why: The kit's own manual requires an earth-ground connection on the trackball and its mounting plate separate from signal wiring; skipping it is an electrical defect, not a cosmetic one.
buildPriorities.proof: A continuity/ground check passes on the trackball and mounting plate independent of the signal harness.

buildPriorities.title: Verify display mode before trusting a widescreen mount
buildPriorities.why: The 2009 manual warns that its software is not designed for a true 16:9 aspect ratio and can appear stretched or skewed on larger HDTVs.
buildPriorities.proof: The selected game and DIP-switch mode are observed on the actual panel. Any distortion is documented and accepted or the display choice changes; a cable or setting alone is not proof of correct geometry.

releaseNotes.title: 2009 kit vs. 2007 Bowler's Club
releaseNotes.body: This page documents the classic landscape Silver Strike Bowling 2009 offline kit: Start, Ball Weight, Overhead, Rotate Left, Rotate Right. The 2007 Bowler's Club release used the same five controls but labeled the ball-selection button Change Ball instead of Ball Weight — a confirmed label difference, not a typo.

releaseNotes.title: League Night is a different product, not a newer build of this one
releaseNotes.body: Silver Strike Bowling: League Night Home Edition is a ground-up reboot on a vertical/portrait monitor with a new engine, touchscreen, NFC and an online subscription that turns paid after Spring 2027; the manufacturer's own store page states it does not include a TV. It is not the classic landscape game pictured and described on this page.

releaseNotes.title: The available gameplay images are small
releaseNotes.body: The checked Arcade Database, GameFAQs, Giant Bomb, Aurcade and alternate flyer sources did not yield higher-resolution authentic gameplay images. This does not prove that none exist elsewhere. The gallery preserves the small flyer crops without inventing detail or claiming they are new captures.

releaseNotes.title: Ownership is not the complete rights check
releaseNotes.body: The 2009 kit manual's license refers to authorized Silver Strike cabinets and commercial locations. Buying a donor does not by itself establish permission for every proposed home use; confirm the selected release's terms before the build gate.
